name: WY at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: Wyoming's R+23 partisan lean makes any Democratic win extremely unlikely
Chuck Gray has a large financial edge, with $1.6M raised plus outside support versus negligible Democratic fundraising
Prediction markets price Republican chances at 99%
Open seat removes incumbency effects but does not threaten Republican hold
model.rationale: Wyoming's R+23 lean, Gray's dominant fundraising and outside backing, and markets pricing the race at 99% Republican all point to a safe Republican hold despite the open seat. The Democrat has raised almost nothing, leaving no realistic path to competitiveness.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected third-party surge could shave the margin, but nothing suggests the seat is in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Harriet Hageman (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Wyoming's at-large House seat is among the most Republican-leaning in the country, with a partisan lean of R+23. Harriet Hageman is leaving the seat to run for Senate, and Chuck Gray enters the general as the heavy favorite after raising over $1.6 million and drawing substantial outside support. Lisa Kinney, the Democratic nominee, has raised under $20,000, and minor-party candidates lack visible resources.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Republicans a 99% chance of holding the seat. The forecast expects a comfortable Republican win in the low-to-mid twenties, consistent with the district's fundamentals and the lopsided resource gap.
